Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.llm.openai

Class OpenAiChatClientAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.llm.openai.OpenAiChatClientAdapter
All Implemented Interfaces:
LlmChatClient
@Component @ConditionalOnBean(org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel.class) public class OpenAiChatClientAdapter extends Object implements LlmChatClient
OpenAI implementation of LlmChatClient (design §12, EPIC-09).

Sits behind Spring AI's ChatModel bean (auto-configured by spring-ai-starter-model-openai). The adapter owns translation of application-layer ChatRequest into Spring AI's Prompt + ChatOptions via OpenAiChatOptionsTranslator, and translation of every provider failure into LlmUnavailableException via OpenAiErrorMapper (REQ-LLM-005).

Tool wiring per agent: for every ToolDescriptor in ChatRequest.tools(), the adapter resolves the underlying @ToolGroup bean from the ToolCatalog and attaches it via OpenAiChatOptionsTranslator as a Spring AI ToolCallback. Spring AI then advertises the @Tool-annotated methods to the LLM and dispatches incoming tool calls back to the bean.

MCP wiring per agent: agent.enabledMcpServers is resolved via McpToolCallbackResolver to the subset of Spring AI MCP ToolCallbacks contributed by the enabled connections (REQ-AGT-009 / REQ-MCP-004). Those callbacks are merged with the static tool-catalog callbacks and attached to OpenAiChatOptions through OpenAiChatOptionsTranslator, so the LLM sees the union of tools and MCP-exposed capabilities on every turn — REQ-AGT-014 stays live because the agent is re-fetched by ChatRequestBuilder on each call.

ConditionalOnBean on ChatModel: in test profiles the OpenAI autoconfig is excluded (Spring AI 1.1.0 / Spring Framework 7 binary incompat) and no ChatModel bean exists. Without the conditional, every @SpringBootTest in the suite would fail to refresh because the adapter cannot satisfy its constructor argument. Tests that need an LlmChatClient bean provide their own ChatModel bean via @TestConfiguration.
